title: A Thorn for the Crown
premise: Ulyana Okonkwo fled her hedge-witch mistress with nothing but a stolen grimoire and a talent for arithmetic, finding refuge as ledger-keeper for the Gilded Thorn, a guild that trades in impossible things: bottled memories, borrowed luck, one honest lie. When the old gods begin answering prayers again after three centuries of silence, every miracle the guild ever sold comes due, and Ulyana discovers her own name written in the oldest ledger — her soul pawned before she was born. With a disgraced guild enforcer, a god's forgotten daughter, and a debt-collector who has fallen out of love with his work, she descends into the court beneath the mountain to steal back what was sold. They succeed only by paying the one price no ledger can hold: the guild itself, dissolved and given away, its found family choosing each other over the trade that bound them.
about_author: Marguerite Underhill is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing merchant ledgers from abandoned mountain towns before turning to fiction. She writes fantasy about people who do the math on miracles and refuse to accept the sum.

chapters.title: The Arithmetic of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. She balances the Gilded Thorn's ledgers by candlelight, introducing the guild's strange inventory and its iron rule: everything is owed. A prayer candle flickers without being lit. Emotional beat: wary contentment in a life built on careful books.

chapters.title: What the Guild Sells
chapters.summary: Ulyana tours the vaults with Vespera, the guildmother, cataloguing bottled memories and a jar of last summer. She notices an entry in a ledger older than the guild itself, written in her own handwriting she never wrote. Beat: unease beneath routine.

chapters.title: A Prayer Answered
chapters.summary: A customer's desperate prayer is answered on the spot — rain of fish, witnessed by half the street. The old gods are awake. Ulyana's POV; beat: wonder curdling into dread as impossible trades begin returning dividends.

chapters.title: The Enforcer at the Door
chapters.summary: Davor Kestrel arrives, a guild enforcer cashiered for refusing to collect a child's debt, seeking shelter. Ulyana vouches for him against Vespera's cold arithmetic. Beat: first spark of loyalty outside the rules.

chapters.title: Ledger of Souls
chapters.summary: Ulyana deciphers the ancient page: souls pawned across generations, hers among them, sold to the court beneath the mountain by her hedge-witch mistress. POV Ulyana. Beat: betrayal and vertigo — her whole self was collateral.

chapters.title: Vespera's Bargain
chapters.summary: Vespera reveals the guild's founding debt to the under-court and offers Ulyana a trade: serve out her soul's term or find a substitute asset. Ulyana refuses. Beat: quiet defiance; the family begins to crack along its ledgers.

chapters.title: The Debt-Collector Who Quit
chapters.summary: Davor's POV. His former partner, Ilya, still collecting for the under-court, warns him to walk away. Flashback to the child he refused to ruin. Beat: guilt sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Winter Comes Early
chapters.summary: The long winter begins falling out of season — snow in harvest month, prayers answered cruelly. The city panics; the guild's stock soars. Ulyana watches greed bloom in the cold. Beat: moral nausea.

chapters.title: The God's Forgotten Daughter
chapters.summary: A girl named Sable breaks into the vaults seeking a bottled memory of her father — a minor god who traded his children's names away. Ulyana hides her. Beat: recognition; two orphans of other people's bargains.

chapters.title: Terms of Descent
chapters.summary: The trio plans the theft of Ulyana's soul from the under-court. Vespera demands the guild take a cut. Davor knows the mountain roads from his collecting days. Beat: uneasy alliance forged over maps and candlelight.

chapters.title: What the Hedge-Witch Kept
chapters.summary: Ulyana returns to her old mistress's cottage to confront her past and finds it burned, the witch gone ahead to the court to collect interest. Only the original contract remains. Beat: grief transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: The Road Under the World
chapters.summary: Descent through the salt tunnels. Davor leads; Sable's divine blood makes lamps burn blue where gods once walked. First ambush by toll-wights demanding payment in years. Beat: fear becoming trust.

chapters.title: Toll
chapters.summary: The wights take three days of Davor's life as passage. He pays without telling them the cost until after. Ulyana rages; he shrugs. Beat: the ethics of sacrifice argued in the dark.

chapters.title: The Market of Small Mercies
chapters.summary: An underground bazaar where prayers are bought and resold. Sable finds a vendor selling her father's voice in a locket. They buy it with Ulyana's last coin. Beat: tenderness amid commerce.

chapters.title: Ilya
chapters.summary: Davor's old partner catches them, torn between duty and affection. He lets them pass but marks their route for the court. Beat: heartbreak; betrayal that isn't quite betrayal.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: Arrival at the under-court: a cathedral of frozen petitions where the old gods sit in judgment of their own debts. Ulyana sees her soul — a small flame in a glass reliquary. Beat: awe and terror.

chapters.title: Audience with the Sleeping Judge
chapters.summary: The chief god wakes groggily, annoyed at being prayed to again. He explains the winter: the gods answer prayers because mortals stopped paying any other way. Beat: dark comedy; cosmic bookkeeping revealed.

chapters.title: Reading the Fine Print
chapters.summary: Ulyana, the guild's auditor, examines her own contract and finds a flaw: the hedge-witch sold a soul she never legally owned — apprenticeship papers were forged. Beat: hope kindled by literacy.

chapters.title: The Court Rejects the Claim
chapters.summary: The judge dismisses the flaw; precedent outweighs truth. Trial set for midwinter's end — when the long winter finishes falling and all outstanding souls revert. Beat: despair, then Sable's hand in hers.

chapters.title: Cells of Glass
chapters.summary: Imprisoned pending trial, the three plan from adjacent cells via tapped code. Davor confesses the full story of the child he saved. Beat: intimacy born of confinement.

chapters.title: Sable's Inheritance
chapters.summary: Sable is recognized by the court as a god's daughter and offered her father's old seat if she renounces her mortal friends. She refuses publicly. Beat: found family chosen over blood and divinity.

chapters.title: The Escape That Wasn't
chapters.summary: They break out using Ulyana's lock-picking-by-ledger trick, but Ulyana doubles back for another prisoner: a child whose soul was pawned like hers. Beat: Davor's old choice replayed, made right this time.

chapters.title: Hunted Through the Halls of Debt
chapters.summary: Flight through the court's archive-mazes, pursued by Ilya and bailiff-spirits. The rescued child slows them; Ulyana refuses to abandon her. Beat: chase tension welded to principle.

chapters.title: The Price of the Door
chapters.summary: The exit gate demands a soul's weight. Davor moves to pay; Ulyana stops him and instead offers the stolen grimoire — her last tie to her old life. Beat: letting go of the past to save the present.

chapters.title: Above Ground, Below Hope
chapters.summary: They surface into deepening winter. The city starves while the guild profits. Ulyana confronts Vespera, who admits she helped forge the apprenticeship papers decades ago. Beat: fury and a terrible understanding.

chapters.title: Vespera's Confession
chapters.summary: Vespera's POV chapter. Her own soul was the guild's first collateral; she has been buying time ever since, and Ulyana was meant to be her replacement. Beat: villainy reframed as survival; pity without absolution.

chapters.title: The Guild Divided
chapters.summary: Guild members split: some side with Vespera's arithmetic, others with Ulyana's refusal. A vote is called on whether to surrender Ulyana to the court. Beat: the found family fracturing under pressure.

chapters.title: The Vote
chapters.summary: The guild votes narrowly to protect Ulyana. Vespera concedes — then vanishes with the oldest ledger, heading for the mountain to cut her own deal. Beat: victory shadowed by loss.

chapters.title: Chasing the Ledger
chapters.summary: Pursuit through blizzard to the mountain's mouth. Ilya intercepts them again — and this time joins them, bringing the court's secret procedures memorized. Beat: redemption accepted awkwardly.

chapters.title: Midwinter's Eve
chapters.summary: They re-enter the court on the eve of reckoning. The hedge-witch waits at the threshold, offering Ulyana freedom in exchange for taking Vespera's place. Beat: temptation offered in the voice of motherhood.

chapters.title: The Refusal
chapters.summary: Ulyana refuses both women's bargains and instead files a formal audit of the entire under-court's accounts — every god's debts, every forged contract, read aloud. Beat: audacity as climax approach; the courtroom freezes.

chapters.title: Trial by Ledger
chapters.summary: The audit exposes that the gods themselves defaulted first — the winter is their repossession of worship. The judge must either admit insolvency or accept restructuring. Beat: rising climax; justice outside the law via bookkeeping.

chapters.title: What No Ledger Can Hold
chapters.summary: The court demands payment anyway. Ulyana offers the only unencumbered asset: the Gilded Thorn itself, dissolved, its impossible inventory returned to the world freely. Beat: sacrifice of the institution that sheltered her.

chapters.title: The Long Winter Breaks
chapters.summary: Debts forgiven, the gods sleep again; the snow slackens. Ulyana's soul-flame is released into her keeping — hers now, unowned. Beat: catharsis; light returning literally and emotionally.

chapters.title: Settlements
chapters.summary: Aftermath above ground: the guild's goods distributed, debts struck from books, customers bewildered by gifts. Davor plants a garden on the vault site. Beat: gentle humor and grief for what was lost.

chapters.title: Vespera's Last Entry
chapters.summary: Vespera, freed of her own contract by the dissolution, walks into the mountains alone but leaves Ulyana the oldest ledger with a final entry: 'paid in full.' Beat: complicated mourning for a mentor.

chapters.title: Sable's Father
chapters.summary: Sable uses the locket of her father's voice for one conversation before it empties. He remembers her name. She lets the locket go. Beat: bittersweet closure of the inheritance theme.

chapters.title: The New Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Spring. Ulyana opens a free counting-house teaching the poor to read contracts, with Davor, Sable, and Ilya beside her. A prayer candle flickers; they let it gutter unanswered. Beat: peace chosen over power.

chapters.title: Entries in a New Book
chapters.summary: Ulyana begins a fresh ledger recording not debts but gifts given and repaid in kindness. Each companion contributes a first entry. Beat: warmth; the found family writing its own terms.

chapters.title: A Thorn for the Crown
chapters.summary: Final image: the crown of the under-court sends an envoy offering Ulyana a title for her services. She uses the envoy's visit to negotiate protections for pawned children, then sends him home. Beat: sovereignty claimed quietly; the thorn kept, the crown declined.
